text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after surging 4.8% yesterday to $463—a pullback from an inflated price following yesterday's news that the U.S. struck a deal with Russia to import diesel. The stock is giving back some of those gains now, likely as investors process the longer-term implications: a flood of cheap Russian diesel into global markets would undercut refiner margins (the profit they make on each barrel processed), which is the core business model for a company like this. Even though U.S. refineries are running hot at 92.7% capacity and diesel inventories are tight, the promise of foreign supply removes the scarcity premium that has been driving profitability.

The broader backdrop underscores why this deal matters: Middle Eastern conflicts, including tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Hurricane Isaias disrupting Gulf of Mexico output, had tightened diesel supplies and boosted prices—a windfall for refiners. An influx of Russian fuel short-circuits that advantage, which is likely why the initial euphoria yesterday didn't stick.
